genesis.41.p1.b1.text: After two full years had passed, Pharaoh had a dream: He was standing beside the Nile, when seven cows, sleek and well-fed, came up from the river and began to graze among the reeds.

genesis.41.p1.b2.text: After them, seven other cows, sickly and thin, came up from the Nile …

genesis.41.p1.b3.text: And the cows that were sickly and thin devoured the seven sleek, well-fed cows.

genesis.41.p2.b1.text: but he fell back asleep and dreamed a second time: Seven heads of grain, plump and ripe, came up on one stalk.

genesis.41.p2.b2.text: And the thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven plump, ripe ones. Then Pharaoh awoke and realized it was a dream.

genesis.41.p2.b3.text: In the morning his spirit was troubled, so he summoned all the magicians and wise men of Egypt.

genesis.41.p2.b4.text: … but no one could interpret them for him.

genesis.41.p3.b2.text: Pharaoh was once angry with his servants, and he put me and the chief baker in the custody of the captain of the guard. One night both the chief baker and I had dreams …

genesis.41.p3.b3.text: Now a young Hebrew was there with us, a servant of the captain of the guard. We told him our dreams and he interpreted them for us individually.

genesis.41.p3.b4.text: And it happened to us just as he had interpreted: I was restored to my position, and the other man was hanged.”

genesis.41.p4.b2.text: who was quickly brought out of the dungeon.

genesis.41.p4.b3.text: After he had shaved and changed his clothes,

genesis.41.p5.b1.text: I had a dream, and no one can interpret it. But I have heard it said of you that when you hear a dream you can interpret it.

genesis.41.p5.b2.text: I myself cannot do it … but God will give Pharaoh a sound answer.

genesis.41.p6.b1.text: In my dream I was standing on the bank of the Nile, when seven cows, well-fed and sleek, came up from the river and began to graze among the reeds.

genesis.41.p6.b2.text: … I have never seen such ugly cows in all the land of Egypt!

genesis.41.p6.b3.text: When they had devoured them, however, no one could tell that they had done so; their appearance was as ugly as it had been before.

genesis.41.p6.b4.text: I told this dream to the magicians, but no one could explain it to me.

genesis.41.p7.b1.text: The dreams of Pharaoh are one and the same. God has revealed to Pharaoh what He is about to do.

genesis.41.p7.b2.text: The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven ripe heads of grain are seven years. The dreams have the same meaning.

genesis.41.p7.b3.text: Behold, seven years of great abundance are coming throughout the land of Egypt, but seven years of famine will follow them. … and the famine will devastate the land.

genesis.41.p7.b4.text: Moreover, because the dream was given to Pharaoh in two versions, the matter has been decreed by God, and He will carry it out shortly.

genesis.41.p8.b1.text: Now, therefore, Pharaoh should look for a discerning and wise man and set him over the land of Egypt.

genesis.41.p8.b2.text: … to take a fifth of the harvest of Egypt during the seven years of abundance.

genesis.41.p8.b3.text: … let them collect all the excess food from these good years, that they may come and lay up the grain to be preserved as food in the cities.

genesis.41.p8.b4.text: This food will be a reserve for the land during the seven years of famine to come upon the land of Egypt. Then the country will not perish in the famine.”

genesis.41.p9.b1.text: This proposal pleased Pharaoh and all his officials.

genesis.41.p9.b2.text: Can we find anyone like this man, in whom the Spirit of God abides?

genesis.41.p9.b3.text: You shall be in charge of my house, and all my people are to obey your commands. Only with regard to the throne will I be greater than you.”

genesis.41.p9.b4.text: I hereby place you over all the land of Egypt.

genesis.41.p10.b1.text: Then Pharaoh removed the signet ring from his finger, put it on Joseph’s finger,

genesis.41.p10.b2.text: clothed him in garments of fine linen, and placed a gold chain around his neck.

genesis.41.p10.b4.text: I am Pharaoh, but without your permission, no one in all the land of Egypt shall lift his hand or foot.

genesis.41.p11.b1.text: Pharaoh gave Joseph the name Zaphenath-paneah, and he gave him Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, to be his wife.

genesis.41.p11.b2.text: Now Joseph was thirty years old when he entered the service of Pharaoh king of Egypt.

genesis.41.p11.b3.text: During the seven years of abundance, the land brought forth bountifully.

genesis.41.p11.b4.text: So Joseph stored up grain in such abundance, like the sand of the sea, that he stopped keeping track of it; for it was beyond measure.

genesis.41.p12.b1.text: Before the years of famine arrived, two sons were born to Joseph by Asenath …

genesis.41.p12.b2.text: God has made me forget all my hardship and all my father’s household.

genesis.41.p12.b3.text: God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.

genesis.41.p13.b1.text: When the seven years of abundance in the land of Egypt came to an end, the seven years of famine began,

genesis.41.p13.b2.text: Go to Joseph and do whatever he tells you.

genesis.41.p13.b3.text: Joseph opened up all the storehouses and sold grain to the Egyptians;

genesis.41.p13.b4.text: And every nation came to Joseph in Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was severe over all the earth.
